page: UpCloud GPU-64xCPU-320GB-4xRTXPRO6000 is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for highly parallelized compute workloads. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9555 processor with 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs under a KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 320.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, delivering a combined 382 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage attachments, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across both compute and memory subsystems. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, scoring 3717.18 and 236275.73 respectively. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 13367.03 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 465.67 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and vector operations are accelerated by hardware flags including AVX-512 and SHA_NI. In database and application benchmarks, the server handles 223.2 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 44.5 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is optimized for large-scale AI inference, machine learning, and parallel data processing. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier performance, processing 7887.2 tokens per second for prompt processing and 213.78 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model. The lack of local storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. The shared CPU allocation model is balanced by the massive dedicated GPU resources, making it a cost-effective solution for high-density GPU workloads that do not require dedicated non-shared CPU cores.
description: UpCloud GPU-64xCPU-320GB-4xRTXPRO6000 is a high-density GPU-accelerated server designed for parallel computing and machine learning workloads. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9555 processor with 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs, the system includes 320.0 GB of system memory and four NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with 382 GB of total VRAM. It operates on a KVM hypervisor with shared CPU allocation and contains no local storage. Benchmarks show top-tier performance, including 236,275.73 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 7,887.2 tokens per second for medium LLM prompt processing. This server is highly suited for large-scale AI inference, parallel data processing, and complex simulations where massive GPU memory and high memory bandwidth are critical, offering a resource-dense profile without the overhead of local storage.
